solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's enumeration wrong at 6 down, recounted from the answer here

clue.text: Slower on airways to holiday home

indicators.note: something said on air is broadcast and heard, not seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
pad is slang for one's home or flat

explanation.surface: Someone flies off slowly to a holiday home abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on airways' signals a sound-alike: BREAK, said aloud, gives BRAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake pad is the part of a vehicle's braking system that presses on the disc and slows the wheel.

clue.text: Diner eating egg doesn't take a long time

indicators.note: doesn't take the letter means that letter is dropped from what has been built
the restaurant word is eating the egg word, so it goes round it

parts.note: a diner is a cheap restaurant, an eatery
a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: A café customer skips the egg, making the meal drag on.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious diner word is EATER, which leaves a Y short; the full restaurant word, EATERY, is needed before 'doesn't take a' removes the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is endless time, used loosely for any very long wait, an age.

clue.text: Fruit dessert — Brown Betty slices appear

indicators.note: the teapot word slices into, cuts into the middle of, the word for appear

parts.note: to come is to appear or arrive
a Brown Betty is a classic round British teapot, so a pot

explanation.surface: A pudding menu in which a Brown Betty, the baked apple dish, turns up in slices.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown Betty is also a baked apple pudding, which makes it look like part of the dessert; here it is the brown glazed teapot found in many British kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Compote is fruit stewed in syrup and served as a pudding.

clue.text: Note commonly picked up from Pavarotti

indicators.note: picked up means heard, and commonly means in a casual everyday accent, so the singer's voice type is heard as another word

parts.note: Luciano Pavarotti was the famous Italian tenor

explanation.surface: A musical note caught from a Pavarotti performance.
explanation.walkthrough: A TENNER is British slang for a ten-pound banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is a ten-pound banknote, and a banknote is simply called a note in Britain.

clue.text: Master of the illusory lands cape in Surrey town

indicators.note: the cape word lands, is set down, within the town
says where the cape letter lands, inside the town name

parts.note: Esher is a town in Surrey, a county south of London
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A landscape artist settles in a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'landscape' split into two words; 'lands' and 'in' together put C inside ESHER.
explanation.definitionFit: M. C. Escher was the Dutch artist famed for impossible staircases and optical illusions.

clue.text: Lord's address — he's about to lead Orchestra: English National

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is', so the clue says a lord is what the wordplay builds: a viscount and admiral

indicators.note: the first part leads, comes before, the orchestra letters
he is about, goes round, the speech word

parts.note: he's is 'he is', giving the letters of he
an address is a formal speech, an oration
the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra, an English orchestra

explanation.surface: A peer gives a speech before conducting the English National Orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord's' is the definition with 's standing for 'is'; the colon makes 'English' describe the orchestra rather than give its own E.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson was made a viscount, so he is a lord, and he is the famous admiral of Trafalgar.

clue.text: Universal handle, so fixed in minds

definitions.text: Universal handle, so fixed in minds

indicators.note: the home word minds, looks after and holds, the rearranged letters

parts.note: someone who is in is at home
U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: the letters are fixed, put right, into a new order

explanation.surface: A name known to everyone, fixed firmly in people's minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges U with HANDLE and SO to give USEHOLDNA, and 'minds' sets it inside HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a name, and one known universally and remembered by all is a famous one.

clue.text: Every Tom, Dick and Har?

parts.note: the phrase for everyone, every Tom, Dick and Harry, runs to twenty letters; the clue prints eighteen of them, so it shows that fraction of the whole

explanation.walkthrough: Count the letters: the full phrase has 20, the clue stops two short at 18, which is the proportion the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighteen out of twenty is nine tenths, which is a proportion of almost everyone.

clue.text: Result of which check-up, nursing bruises?

definitions.text: Result of which check-up, nursing bruises?

indicators.note: the letters are bruised, battered out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: A medical check-up finds a patient tending bruises, and asks what caused them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bruises' rearranges CHECKUPNURSING. Read whole, the clue asks what kind of blows would leave someone needing a check-up while nursing bruises.
explanation.definitionFit: Landing unexpected, unguarded blows would leave the victim bruised and in need of medical attention.

clue.text: See 8
The Artificial Tongue of Eugene Onegin

indicators.note: the word sits inside, is part of, the opera title

explanation.surface: Reads like the title of a scholarly study of the language in Pushkin's verse novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the gap between eugeNE Onegin.
explanation.definitionFit: Neo is a constructed international language, one of many invented rivals to Esperanto.

clue.text: Ale supplier goes into business with Cheese and Meat Sanctuary

indicators.note: the pub letters go into the middle of the shop word

parts.note: a deli, a delicatessen, is a shop selling cheese and cooked meats
PH is the map abbreviation for public house, a pub that supplies ale

explanation.surface: A brewer teams up with a cheese and meat firm to open a sanctuary.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi was the sacred precinct of Apollo in ancient Greece, home of the oracle.

clue.text: Productivity of the Red Queen's kitchen compound?

parts.note: in Alice the Queen of Hearts made some tarts, so tart stands for what a queen's kitchen produces
productivity is measured as a rate of output

explanation.surface: How fast the royal kitchen in Wonderland turns out its pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the slip that the Queen of Hearts, not the Red Queen, was the one who made tarts in Alice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartrate is a salt or ester of tartaric acid, a chemical compound.

clue.text: A twitch, every now and again

definitions.text: A twitch, every now and again

indicators.note: taking letters every now and again, at intervals, picks alternate ones

explanation.surface: A twitch that comes back from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking alternate letters of 'twitch' gives T, I and C. The whole clue then also describes the answer, a twitch that recurs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tic is an involuntary muscle spasm that recurs at intervals.

clue.text: Somebody rich needing GP for massaging work?

indicators.note: letters handed over for massaging are kneaded and worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wealthy client wants a doctor to give them a massage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for massaging' rearranges SOMEBODYRICH with GP.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodbye, Mr Chips is James Hilton's 1934 novel about a schoolmaster, a literary work.

clue.text: Merging live US track raised sound level

indicators.note: the two words merge, sharing the letter where they meet, so one copy of it goes

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means written upwards, so the railway word reads backwards

parts.note: the el is the elevated railway in American cities

explanation.surface: Mixing a live recording with an American track pushed the volume up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merging' means the two short words overlap on their shared E, so it appears only once.
explanation.definitionFit: The bel is the unit of ten decibels used to measure sound intensity.

clue.text: See 14
Flirty friar collects fine, following female faex populi

indicators.note: the rearranged friar collects, takes inside, the fine letter
flirty suggests letters dancing about, so the friar's letters are rearranged

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A flirtatious monk is fined, chasing after women, a disgrace to the people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flirty' turns FRIAR into RIFRA, and 'collects' puts F inside it to give RIFFRA. 'faex populi' is Latin for 'dregs of the people'.
explanation.definitionFit: Riff-raff means disreputable common people, the rabble; that is the dregs of the populace.

clue.text: Rachel lost one following me cutting across some land

indicators.note: the note cuts across the middle of the rearranged name
lost letters have gone astray, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
in sol-fa, me (mi) is followed by fa

explanation.surface: Rachel lost a friend who followed her across some fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the mi of do-re-mi, so the note after it is fa; 'cutting across' sets it in the middle of the rearranged name.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-acre is a small plot measuring half of the standard unit of land area.

clue.text: Take power up, but not with sailing event

parts.note: R is the abbreviation of Latin recipe, take, used on prescriptions

indicators.note: but not signals that a letter is left out of what has been built
in a down clue up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: wattage is electrical power measured in watts

explanation.surface: Assume command of a ship, except without the sailing contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns WATTAGE round to EGATTAW, and 'but not' drops its W.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat or yacht races held as one event.

clue.text: My slimming having taken effect, your compiler had Listener's cake

parts.note: a setter calls himself I, so the setter had is I had, shortened to I'd

indicators.note: what a listener hears is the sound, not the spelling, of the cake

parts.note: an eclair is a long cream cake

explanation.surface: The diet having worked, the setter treated himself to a cream cake, with an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slimming having taken effect' is scene-setting: a slimmed cake is spelt thinner but sounds the same. The Listener is also a famously hard crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, used interchangeably in speech.

clue.text: Secret court cases are unsuccessful

indicators.note: the court letters case, enclose, the losing word

parts.note: to lose is to be unsuccessful

explanation.surface: In a closed hearing the court's cases fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like legal cases, but is a verb: the court letters encase LOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Closet as an adjective means hidden or private, as in a closet admirer.

clue.text: Toasted sarnie popped up

indicators.note: toasting changes the bread, so these letters are reshaped into a new order; a sarnie is British slang for a sandwich

explanation.surface: A toasted sandwich leaps out of the toaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something that has appeared or emerged, risen into view.

clue.text: Purchasing points all but replete with stuff miles away

indicators.note: all but the word means every letter but its last

parts.note: replete means full

indicators.note: miles away means the miles letter goes from the stuffing word

parts.note: to stuff is to cram

explanation.surface: Shopping spots almost full of goods, far off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchasing' is not buying here: purchase means mechanical grip or leverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulcra are the pivots on which levers turn, the points where they gain mechanical purchase.

clue.text: Good though graphic format

parts.note: if, as in 'fine, if dull', means though

explanation.surface: A decent, if limited, picture file type.
explanation.definitionFit: GIF is the Graphics Interchange Format used for images and short animations.

clue.text: Vorderman, occupying Zone A, is hot stuff!

parts.note: Carol Vorderman is a British TV presenter, famous from the quiz show Countdown
someone occupying a place is in it
a zone is an area
a as in 'twice a day' means per

explanation.surface: A TV presenter in Zone A is declared very attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is not the letter but means 'per', as in so much a head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Carolina Reaper is among the world's hottest chilli peppers, so fiery stuff indeed.

clue.text: See 25
Bilbo's Magnificent Birthday Run that invokes the Lord above?

definitions.meaning: in The Lord of the Rings, Bilbo Baggins throws a grand party for his 111th birthday

definitions.text: Run that invokes the Lord above?
definitions.meaning: a cricket score of 111 is called a Nelson, so that run total calls to mind the lord at 6 across

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a team or batter on 111 is on 'Nelson', named after Horatio Nelson, the answer at 6 across; 'the Lord above' looks like God.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's hobbits say eleventy-one for 111, so the 111th birthday is the eleventy-first, matching the run tally.
